executionFlows.name: Upload full features
executionFlows.summary: Follow an uploaded file through JSON parsing, Azure Blob Storage, Kafka publication and the HTTP response, including the null and failure paths.

steps.title: Receive an authenticated upload
steps.description: POST /api/FullFeatures accepts an uploaded file. The controller requires an authenticated user through the configured JWT bearer policy. The following path starts once authentication and file binding succeed.

evidence.claim: The controller has [Authorize], [Route("api/[controller]")], and [ApiController].
The action is [HttpPost] Upload(IFormFile file), so its route is the controller route with no suffix.
MVC receives a JWT authorization filter requiring an authenticated user and JWT bearer authentication is configured with issuer, audience, lifetime, and HTTPS validation settings.
The request pipeline calls UseAuthentication and UseAuthorization.
The controller is an ApiController, enabling ASP.NET Core API binding/validation conventions.
Upload declares only IFormFile file and immediately logs file.FileName before reading it; no explicit file validation is present in the action.

steps.title: Read the uploaded file
steps.description: The controller opens the file stream and awaits the entire contents as a string. This happens before its handler try/catch, so a file-access or read exception bypasses the HTTP 400 branch.

evidence.claim: Upload calls OpenReadStream, reads to the end asynchronously, and assigns the text to result.

steps.title: Parse the full-features JSON
steps.description: The controller awaits PrinsFullFeaturesMessageHandler.ProcessMessage. It deserializes the text into FullFeatures, including SpecMarket, ModelYear and CarType. A non-null result continues to storage; a null result skips storage and publication and completes normally. Invalid JSON can throw into the failure-storage branch.

evidence.claim: The controller constructor receives IPrinsFullFeaturesMessageHandler and stores it as IMessageHandler.
Upload awaits ProcessMessage(result) inside its try block.
DI registers IPrinsFullFeaturesMessageHandler to PrinsFullFeaturesMessageHandler as scoped.
ProcessMessage deserializes the input string to FullFeatures inside a try block.
FullFeatures defines SpecMarket, ModelYear, CarType, and FullFeaturesContent fields.
Repository SetAsync and PublishMessage are both inside the non-null conditional, with no else or throw for a null result.
After a normally completing handler, Upload logs processed and returns Ok().

steps.title: Save the original JSON in Azure Blob Storage
steps.description: Build the key full-features-{SpecMarket}-{ModelYear}-{CarType}. FullFeaturesRepository stores the original JSON under the full-features directory in the configured PCF container. The blob client encodes it as UTF-8 and awaits UploadAsync with overwrite enabled. Publication starts only after this write completes.

evidence.claim: The handler creates FullFeatureKey from the deserialized SpecMarket, ModelYear, and CarType and stores the original message.
FullFeatureKey builds the full-features prefix key and FullFeaturesRepository uses that prefix as its base path.
Repository stores the configured PCF container name and supplied base path.
Repository.SetAsync awaits the blob client upload with container, base path, key, and content.
BlobStorageClient UTF-8 encodes content, gets the configured container blob, and awaits UploadAsync with overwrite true.
FullFeaturesRepository and FullFeatureFailureRepository are registered as scoped services.
AzureBlobStorage settings are bound and IBlobStorageClient is bound to BlobStorageClient.

steps.title: Build the full-features notification
steps.description: The handler awaits FullFeaturesMessageService.PublishMessage, which calls KafkaNotificationService. It maps SpecMarket, CarType and ModelYear into the protobuf FullFeaturesMessage, adds a message header, and builds the Kafka key SpecMarket-CarType-ModelYear. The message contains identifying fields, not the uploaded file.

evidence.claim: The handler awaits repository persistence and then awaits PublishMessage with SpecMarket, CarType, and ModelYear.
FullFeaturesMessageService obtains the configured FullFeaturesTopicName and awaits Task.WhenAll around PublishKafkaMessage.
The service rethrows one exception and aggregates/logs more than one exception; it has no retry loop.
KafkaNotificationService is constructed with IKafkaProducer and reads FullFeaturesTopicName from Kafka configuration.
Full-features publication builds the protobuf message, header, and composite key, then awaits SendAsync.
BuildFullFeaturesMessage copies SpecMarket, CarType, and ModelYear to the generated protobuf message.
The protobuf contract has spec_market, car_type, and model_year string fields.

steps.title: Await publication to Confluent Kafka
steps.description: ProtoBufKafkaProducer serializes the protobuf value to bytes and attaches the headers. KafkaProducerBase awaits Confluent ProduceAsync using Kafka:FullFeaturesTopicName. The production settings name prod.public.pcf.fullfeatures. The HTTP request waits for this call to complete; downstream consumer processing is outside this trace.

evidence.claim: ProtoBufKafkaProducer is the IKafkaProducer implementation and derives from KafkaProducerBase<byte[]>.
The producer serializes the protobuf value, builds the Kafka message and headers, and awaits base.SendAsync.
KafkaProducerBase initializes an IProducer<string,T> through the factory using Kafka configuration values.
KafkaProducerBase awaits _producer.ProduceAsync and wraps KafkaException after logging details.
The factory validates settings, configures ProducerBuilder handlers, builds the producer, and wraps build failures.
ProducerConfig sets client, bootstrap, SASL credentials/mechanism, and security protocol; SASL values are required for SASL protocols.
ProduceAsync is awaited and KafkaException is rethrown as an Exception after logging.
The constructed ProducerConfig contains connection and security fields but no explicit Acks or retry setting.
The controller awaits handler completion before logging processed and returning Ok().
Production settings name prod.public.pcf.fullfeatures as FullFeaturesTopicName.

steps.title: Return HTTP 200
steps.description: If the handler completes normally, Upload returns Ok(). This covers both successful storage/publication and the null-deserialization branch that skipped them. HTTP 200 does not establish that a downstream Kafka consumer has processed the event.

evidence.claim: Repository SetAsync and PublishMessage are both inside the non-null conditional, with no else or throw for a null result.
After a normally completing handler, Upload logs processed and returns Ok().
File access/read is before the try; handler exceptions are caught, logged, returned as BadRequest(e.Message), and normal completion returns Ok().
Unhandled exceptions escaping the controller pipeline are caught by middleware.
Middleware writes application/problem+json and maps unrecognized exceptions to InternalServerError (HTTP 500); selected validation/core/request failures map to other statuses.

steps.title: Attempt to save the failed input
steps.description: If deserialization, blob persistence or publication throws, the handler attempts to store the original input under full-features-failure with a new GUID key. It awaits that write, then logs and rethrows the original exception. If this failure write also throws, its exception escapes instead. A successful main blob write is not rolled back when later publication fails.

evidence.claim: The handler catches all exceptions, writes the original message to FullFeatureFailureRepository, logs the key, and rethrows.
Failure keys use the full-features-failure prefix plus a new GUID and the repository uses that base path.
Failure repository SetAsync delegates to the same awaited blob upload abstraction.

steps.title: Return HTTP 400 with the exception message
steps.description: Upload catches an exception escaping ProcessMessage, logs it and returns BadRequest(e.Message). This includes the original processing error after successful failure storage, or a replacement error thrown while attempting failure storage.

gaps: Authentication rejection and malformed multipart binding are framework-controlled paths not expanded here. Upload has no explicit file-size, content-type or JSON validation before reading the file.
This is a static trace of the pinned source revision. Awaited storage and producer calls remain part of the same HTTP request; they are not background handoffs.
Kafka consumer processing and deployed broker/client retry or acknowledgment behavior are not established. The inspected producer configuration does not explicitly set acknowledgment or retry policy.
POST /api/FullFeatures/retryFailed is a separate, manually triggered recovery endpoint. A failed upload does not call or schedule it automatically.

gaps.reason: Several controller actions return untyped IActionResult values, so no local response schema can be asserted.
IFormFile uploads and VolvoCars ListResponse/OffsetPagination wrappers are referenced but their definitions are not present in the source snapshot.
No PostgreSQL row expiry, Azure Blob lifecycle policy, Kafka retention, or explicit TTL is defined by the packet; all TTL values are therefore null.

The packet identifies MarketAuth, Features, GlobalDict, and FullFeatures input containers, but complete wire schemas for most raw files are not present; only the explicitly typed market-feature-description NDJSON shape and market-auth blob metadata are reported as input documents.

README.md documents component and componentattribute topics, but the inspected production code exposes only event builders and no active publisher invocation; they are omitted rather than inferred from DTOs or tests.
The internal Azure Blob repositories persist content as strings, so their keys are known but the complete serialized payload schemas cannot be established from the repository contracts.
The blob repositories persist and retrieve opaque UTF-8 strings; packet evidence defines keys and paths but does not establish a schema for each stored payload.
No database row expiry, blob lifecycle policy, or per-record TTL is defined in the packet, so ttl is null for every record.

InboxRepository accepts an arbitrary source key; only the stage folder and file-type-to-container mapping are fixed. Market-authorization monitoring recognizes one filename convention, but that does not constrain all inbound file types.
The packet contains SalesModelEntity, but the current PcfDbContext and current model snapshot do not define a SalesModels table; it is excluded as unverified current persistence.

Early packet migrations create a separate CarConfigs table, but a later packet migration explicitly drops it after CarConfigJson is added to Pno12s; it is excluded as historical rather than current persistence.

Direct entity definitions contain later records or fields not represented by this packet's final migration snapshot; they were excluded because this output is limited to persistence evidenced by the packet.
No TTL or expiry policy is configured for the PostgreSQL records evidenced by this packet.
A SalesModelEntity type exists, but this packet's DbContext and current model snapshot provide no DbSet or table mapping for it, so it is excluded.
The producer uses Confluent client defaults and does not configure retry, acknowledgement, idempotence, or dead-letter behavior.
ComponentCreated/Updated/Deleted and ComponentAttributeCreated/Updated/Deleted contracts/topics are documented, but no active publisher service or configuration binding was found.
Managed broker retention, production partition counts, and server-side dead-letter configuration are outside the repository snapshot.
